st: Put the fish, [[1 stalk]] of the lemongrass, ginger and turmeric in a pot with the water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes until the fish is cooked.
Lift out the fish, let it cool a little, then flake it, discarding skin and bones. Keep the broth.
Toast the chickpea flour in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes, stirring, until it smells nutty. Whisk it with [[1 cup]] of the cooled broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the chopped onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, paprika and the remaining crushed lemongrass and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the flaked fish, banana stem and fish sauce, then pour in the broth.
Slowly stir in the chickpea flour mixture. Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring often, until the soup is thick and rich.
Meanwhile, soak the noodles in hot water for 10 minutes, boil for 2 minutes until soft, and drain.
Fry the sliced onion in a little extra oil until crisp and golden, for garnish.
Put noodles in bowls and ladle the hot soup over them. Top with egg, cilantro, crisp onion and a squeeze of lime.

ing: lahpet, or finely minced pickled green tea
st: Chop the tea leaves a little if they are in big pieces. Squeeze out extra liquid.
In a small bowl, mix the tea leaves with the lime juice, fish sauce and peanut oil.
Let the tea leaf mixture rest for 10 minutes so the flavors blend.
Put the cabbage, tomatoes, chili and dried shrimp in a large bowl.
Place the tea leaf mixture in the center of a serving plate and arrange the cabbage, tomatoes, peanuts, garlic chips, split peas and sesame seeds around it in separate piles.
At the table, toss everything together so each bite has crunch.
Taste and add more lime juice or fish sauce if you like. Eat right away so it stays crisp.
Soak the noodles in hot water for 10 minutes until pliable, then boil for 2 minutes and drain well. Toss with [[1 tbsp]] of the oil.
Heat the remaining [[2 tbsp]] oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic for 1 minute until golden.
Add the chicken, turmeric and salt and cook for 6 minutes, stirring, until no pink remains.
Add the tomatoes, chili flakes, soy sauce and sugar and cook for 8 minutes, mashing the tomatoes, until a thick sauce forms.
Pour in the water and simmer 5 more minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Divide the noodles among bowls and spoon the chicken tomato sauce on top.
Finish with the crushed peanuts, scallions and cilantro. Serve with extra soy sauce or chili on the side.
Toast the chickpea flour in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes. Whisk it with [[1 cup]] of the broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for 8 minutes until golden.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until it loses its pink color.
Pour in the remaining broth, the coconut milk and the fish sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Slowly whisk in the chickpea mixture and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring often, until thick and the chicken is at least 165°F (74°C).
Meanwhile, boil the noodles according to the package, usually 3 minutes, then drain.
Put the noodles into bowls and ladle the hot soup over.
Top with egg halves, cilantro, chili flakes and a squeeze of lime.
Put the onions in a food processor and pulse to a coarse paste, or chop very fine.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 15 minutes, stirring, until it turns deep golden and the oil starts to separate.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric, paprika, chili powder and salt for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until jammy.
Add the chicken and turn it in the paste. Cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, cover, and simmer on low for 35 minutes, turning the chicken now and then.
The chicken should reach 165°F (74°C) and a layer of red oil should rise on top, which is traditional.
Scatter with cilantro and serve with rice.
Toast the chickpea flour in a dry pan for 3 minutes until fragrant, then whisk with [[0.5 cup]] of the water.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and cook half of the sliced onion for 8 minutes until golden. Take out half of the oil and onions for the noodles.
To the pan, add the garlic, turmeric and paprika for 1 minute, then add the chicken.
Cook the chicken for 5 minutes. Add the remaining [[0.5 cup]] water, the fish sauce and the chickpea mixture.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring, until the chicken is cooked to 165°F (74°C) and the curry is thick.
Cook the noodles in boiling water until tender, about 6 minutes, then drain.
Toss the noodles with the reserved onion oil, lime juice, chili flakes and a pinch of salt from the table.
Top the noodles with the chicken curry, the egg slices, the remaining raw onion, cilantro and scallions. Mix before eating.
For the broth, simmer the split peas with [[3 cups]] of water, the turmeric and garlic for 25 minutes until very soft.
Mash the peas with a fork and thin with a little hot water to make a pourable broth. Stir in the salt and the fish sauce.
Warm the samosas in a 375°F (190°C) oven for 8 minutes so they are crisp.
Break the samosas into bite-size pieces on a large plate.
Top with the chickpeas, cabbage, red onion, mint and cilantro.
Spoon the warm split pea broth over the top.
Sprinkle with chili flakes and lime juice, toss lightly, and serve right away.

ing: quail eggs or small eggs, see steps
st: Whisk the rice flour, cooked rice, water, coconut milk and salt into a smooth batter, like thin pancake batter. Rest for 15 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar and chili flakes in a small bowl for the dipping sauce.
Heat a nonstick pan with round dimples, or a small nonstick skillet, over medium heat. Brush each hollow with a little oil.
Pour the batter into each hollow until two-thirds full. Cover and cook for 3 minutes.
Add a few chickpeas, some onion and scallions on top. Crack an egg onto each, or whisk the eggs and spoon about [[1 tbsp]] over each.
Cover and cook for 5 minutes until the base is crisp and golden and the egg is fully set.
Slide each pancake out with a spoon. Join two together to form the husband and wife pair if using dimples.
Serve hot with the dipping sauce.
Boil [[2 cups]] of the water in a pot. Add the sago and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often, until the pearls turn clear. Drain and rinse under cold water.
For the jelly, whisk the agar with [[1 cup]] of the water and [[0.25 cup]] of the sugar in a small pot. Bring to a boil and simmer for 2 minutes.
Pour the jelly into a shallow dish, tint with coloring if you like, and chill for 20 minutes until firm. Cut into small cubes.
Toast the bread cubes in a 350°F (175°C) oven for 8 minutes until lightly golden and dry.
Warm the coconut milk with the remaining [[0.5 cup]] sugar, the salt and the pandan or vanilla for 5 minutes, stirring, until the sugar dissolves. Do not boil hard.
Cool the coconut mixture, then chill it until cold.
Put sago, jelly cubes and bread in bowls. Pour over the cold coconut milk and add ice.
